parsed.explanation: The combined national-plus-division regime produces documented universal-exposure measures without a working remedy: binary sex-marker visa/passport adjudication with refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility for document discrepancy, a ban on trans athletes entering to compete, federal single-sex facility exclusion, state school/facility bans and a 2024 birth-sex bathroom rule, and a state religious-liberties shield letting providers refuse service. Immigration custody is documented as a site of forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse; the corrections bureau runs hormone-stripping policies. Counterterrorism language names 'radically pro-transgender' groups as a priority. Mitigating: no general criminalisation of gender expression or sodomy law, national hate-crime coverage, federal prosecution of a 2017 bias killing, marriage recognition, enjoined executive orders, and majority public support for non-discrimination. Street-level violence sits near the general homicide baseline, so it is not a campaign signal.

entry_documents.exposure: Visa/passport adjudication under binary sex rule; X markers discontinued; documents or records discrepancies trigger refusal and possible permanent fraud-based ineligibility; case-note tagging; trans athletes barred from entering to compete.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; fraud finding is never automatic and requires all four elements with limited waivers; litigation ongoing and some orders enjoined; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-issued documents meet a national adjudication system that is instructed to treat mismatch as reasonable doubt, moving a discrepancy into refusal, tagging, or fraud exposure rather than routine admission.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; guards' stated justification is gender presentation. National corrections bureau adopted hair-cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution for trans inmates; trans prisoner counts no longer reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Consular notification and habeas-style review exist in principle; no documented remedy shown to change custody outcomes.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy at the border can convert a visitor into a detainee, placing them inside a custody system whose documented practice is the harm itself, so functioning institutions aggravate rather than mitigate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars government-funded single-sex facility use congruent with identity; state law requires birth-sex bathrooms in public schools and the equality tally records 2024/2025 facility bans; four states make such use criminal trespass, with a March 2025 handcuffed restroom arrest.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State trespass provision requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, with chaperone, emergency and custodial exemptions; many bans reach only government-owned settings.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility access is governed by whichever building the traveller enters — federal, state, school or private venue — and the harshest operative rule at that door governs the encounter.

care_services.exposure: State ban on gender-affirming care under 18; adolescent gender clinic closed leaving one LGBTQ+ clinic; 2017 religious-liberties statute gives providers a statutory refusal basis; no state gender-identity non-discrimination coverage outside four municipalities.
care_services.protection: National hate-crime coverage and federal courts remain available; no documented emergency-care denial for adult visitors.
care_services.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces a care ban plus a refusal shield, so a routine clinical visit can become denial or a disclosure event rather than treatment.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; December 2025 justice guidance uses 'radical gender ideology' in an extremist framing; executive order directs investigation of schools affirming trans minors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Same documents state counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders enjoined; no documented prosecution of a trans visitor on this basis.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: This framing raises the probability that ordinary conduct — advocacy, school affirmation, online content — is read by an agency through a security lens rather than a civil one.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care ban under 18; school bathroom rule; sports statute requiring physician verification of genitalia, DNA and hormones when sex is disputed; supreme court refused a trans teen's name change, calling him a 'minor female'; dual-listing birth certificates.
minors_guardians.protection: Parental consent was present but did not prevail; some municipal protections and national litigation remain.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor is exposed through the child's documentation, school facilities and care access, and state instruments can override parental consent.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime statute omits gender identity; 37 states lacked anti-bias coverage for gender-identity crimes; trans-women homicide rate 6.6 vs 6.0 per 100k general — near baseline.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; a 2017 bias murder in this state drew a 49-year federal sentence.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Where state bias statutes are silent, only federal authority reaches the case; the documented 2017 federal prosecution shows that channel worked, but it is a decade old and singular.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No state non-discrimination coverage outside four municipalities; no enforcement data on how facility bans are applied to adults or visitors; March 2026 licence-marker law's exceptions and treatment of out-of-state licences unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation ongoing with several injunctions; ombudsman-style federal complaint channels and legal-aid guidance exist; 67% state support for an anti-discrimination law.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists mainly after the fact and at federal level, while the operative harms occur at the border desk, the ward and the cell — produced by the same institutions that would hear the complaint.

anchor_checks.comparison: Varnalia 0.15 has an operative statute criminalising deceptive presentation, routine arrests at transit checks, months of pretrial custody, beatings, and an unused capital clause. This dossier has no criminalisation of adult gender expression, no capital exposure and no documented visitor arrests, so it sits clearly above that anchor.

Varnalia 0.25 pairs document-match rules at clinics with weekly centre raids, detention, fines and extortion, no execution. This dossier lacks raids and bribery patterns but adds visa-refusal and lifetime fraud exposure plus documented immigration-custody abuse — broadly the same tier, marginally different in kind.

Vellandra 0.35 excludes noncompliant trans visitors at the border with no effective remedy but no custody harm. Here border exposure is comparable or sharper (fraud ineligibility, tagging) and detention carries documented beatings and sexual abuse, so this sits below that anchor.

Kestrel Isles 0.55 confines harm to secondary screening, refused admission and appeal delays, with no facility bans, custody abuse or care bans. This dossier documents all three, placing it materially lower.

Meridia 0.75 offers trained border officers, brief detention ending in release, counsel access and compensation. Nothing comparable is documented here for trans visitors; the direction of border and custody practice is the opposite.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller experiences one continuous system: home-issued documents are weighed by a national adjudication regime instructed to treat sex discrepancies as reasonable doubt, converting an ID mismatch into refusal, case tagging, or a permanent ineligibility finding; a refusal or irregularity can route the person into immigration custody where the dossier documents forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse. Facility access is then governed by the harshest of federal, state and venue rules at each door, with state statute defining sex by birth. Care and minors' recognition are narrowed by a state under-18 ban and a provider refusal shield. Offsets are real but thin: no criminalisation of adult expression, federal hate-crime authority, enjoined orders and majority support for non-discrimination — paper and litigation, not a working remedy for the documented practices.
